question: Should `openclaw browser fill --fields-file` reject all valid JSON descriptor files above 1 MiB as a permanent public CLI contract?
rationale: The implementation is mechanically coherent, but selecting a fixed maximum changes an existing CLI input contract and can break automation that previously accepted larger valid files; source and proof establish behavior, not approval of that compatibility tradeoff.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB contract
options.body: Accept the documented ceiling as the supported Browser CLI limit and merge with the existing exact-boundary and oversize coverage.

options.title: Preserve existing valid-file compatibility
options.body: Replace the unconditional new rejection with an approach that bounds resource use without making previously accepted descriptor files fail, or add an explicitly approved compatibility path.

options.title: Set a different supported limit
options.body: Choose and document a different owner-approved maximum, then update the help text, docs, proof, and boundary tests together.

recommendation.title: Preserve existing valid-file compatibility
recommendation.body: Replace the unconditional new rejection with an approach that bounds resource use without making previously accepted descriptor files fail, or add an explicitly approved compatibility path.

likelyOwner.reason: They can explain the intended cap and revise the proposal, while a current-main area owner should make the final compatibility decision.
